newsitem.title: USA: SyQuest starts delivery of new disk drive.
newsitem.headline: SyQuest starts delivery of new disk drive.

text.p: SyQuest Technology Inc, a maker of computer storage devices, said it has begun delivery of its new SyJet 1.5 gigabyte removable cartridge disk drive with volume shipments expected to begin in January.
In addition, the company said it has shipped over 90,000 units of its new EZFlyer 230 disk drive, the second of its EZ product family.

Earlier on Tuesday, SyQuest reported a loss of $1.29 a share on revenue of $44.8 million for its fourth quarter ended September 30 versus a loss of $1.69 a share on revenue of $88.4 million one year ago.
Though SyQuest's 1996 fourth quarter revenues were almost one-half the 1995 figure, they represent an increase of over $15 million from the third quarter's $29.5 million.

"This quarter is a benchmark in our turnaround strategy," Chairman Ed Marinaro said in a statement. "(It) marks the first time in over a year that the company has achieved sequential quarterly revenue growth."

SyQuest has seen its market share decline in the last year from new competitors in the computer storage business such as Iomega Corp, a maker of optical drives including the Zip drive. The company has been putting out new products in an effort to meet competition.
Its stock price has fallen from a high of 17-1/4 in mid-May to its current trading range around 4. SyQuest shares were off 4/16 at 3-11/16 by midday.
In its statement, SyQuest also said it has "significantly restored its balance sheet" by completing $71.5 million in new equity investments and restructuring $38.5 million of debt.
